spans.s:
kheṭaka
(‘that which produces fear’)
------------------------------------------
Though, literally, it indicates any weapon that strikes terror in the minds of enemies, the word is normally applied for a shield (used along with a sword). It has a handle at the back to hold it and the front may have artistic designs.
Many Hindu deities hold it in one of their hands.
In Durgāpūja, the खेटक is also offered special worship.
Sometimes, the club wielded by बलराम, is also called Kheṭa or खेटक.
